item.title: Re: Memetic Instruction Pamphlets
item.content:encoded: Great feedback. I also completely agree with you on the anomaly part. I really like the story, but I just can't make a good anomaly to go with it. I'm going to make it a tale. Thanks for your time!

item.title: Re: Memetic Instruction Pamphlets
item.content:encoded:
The whole "this anomaly makes you do bad things to other people" is so played out that I would be unlikely to find it particularly interesting. More so the whole "hidden group that knows more than the foundation and will be watching" brand new GoI.

I think at its core, this concept proposal shows that you know how to tell a story as the investigation sounds somewhat compelling but the core anomaly is sorta cliche…

I'd suggest going back to the drawing board as to the actual anomaly, because this just covers tropes that are too frequently leaned on in my opinion.

item.title: Re: Memetic Conversation Cards
item.content:encoded:
Great criticism, as always. I was thinking of fleshing the idea out a little more, maybe making a PoI or a GoI that created these as a form of getting what they want.
I was a little unclear on what 'to the researchers' meant. I wrote it as they thought it was mostly harmless to the D-Class who tested on it.

I've reworked the concept to be more mysterious and less 'malicious item is malicious.'

Edit for all future reviewers: this exchange happened before I revised the concept, so some of the comments made won't make sense. Cheers!

item.title: Re: Memetic Conversation Cards
item.content:encoded:
+ Cope Crit
- Close

Let's see what we have here…

A set of ever-changing anomalous conversation cards that compel the reader to do whatever the card has written on it- for example, if one said "read this card over and over", the subject would be forced to read the card over and over until the cards are taken from them or they expire.

Mind-affecting objects have been done before, but that doesn't mean you can't put another spin on it. let's see the narrative shall we?

A group of researchers testing the capabilities of the SCP after MTF recovery units with memetic resistance read the cards and are forced to do the actions on the cards, requiring a second team to come in. They are located in a house with a family who is also stuck performing the acts described by the cards. The researchers have extensive testing logs in which they test the capabilities of the cards, ending in a scenario where the last card says "Cause a containment breach at Site-██. " The result box says nothing but [DATA EXPUNGED] resulting in ██ casualties. Testing on SCP-XXXX halted indefinitely.

Okay, this seems kinda boring. So it's only purpose in the narrative is to cause a attainment breach at the end. I mean, the card idea is kinda interesting, depending vastly on what the cards show. I also feel like the last;

ending in a scenario where the last card says "Cause a containment breach at Site-██. " The result box says nothing but [DATA EXPUNGED] resulting in ██ casualties. Testing on SCP-XXXX halted indefinitely.

is kinda pointless. I personally don't see why they would have any Foundation personnel using this mind-affecting item, instead per say, a D-Class. I also doubt a D-Class could do much damage.

Although the SCP seems harmless to the researchers at first, the cards in the testing log become more and more malicious as time goes on.

I still don't understand why researchers would use themselves as subjects to the cards in the first place. Even if they did, once testing started to become more malicious I feel like D-Class would come in anyways.

The cards then convey a message to the researchers, ending in something like I KNOW YOU'RE READING THIS : GET AWAY FROM MY CARDS : [EXPLETIVE REMOVED] YOU : Cause a containment breach at Site-██.

Are the cards sapient? If so, why do they do what they do? Are they one entity? Is someone controlling them? Why do the cards exist? If they're just here to make people go crazy and do harmful actions, I just find that boring. Unless you have narrative of course.

Overall Thoughts: "Overall, this has some substance and little to no narrative. First, I suggest you think more about this idea overall. It needs more. So far this is just a thing that does a thing for no reason. That's fine I guess, but very boring. Narrative is what drives a story forward. So, what is the narrative? Did someone create the cards? Are the cards someone? Maybe the cards are an entity's eyes? Also, why are the cards basically evil? Do they have any reason to be? Once you answer these questions, I believe you can go somewhere with this idea. Hope your concept gets better man. PM me if you need help with the concept.

- Close

item.title: Explosive Gift Mug
item.content:encoded:
A gift mug that painfully bonds to human skin and explodes with the force of a small bomb, severely injuring or killing the one who touched it.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Mystery

Elevator Pitch: A mug that, when touched by human skin, bonds to the skin and explodes with a force beyond what a normal mug would. The mug then reforms over a period of 24 hours. The mugs are used in murder attempts, disguised as gifts, and the Foundation has to find out who is trying to kill the targets and why.

Central Narrative: The mugs are delivered to seemingly random homes in urban areas such as Berlin, NYC, and London. Interviews with the owners of the homes show that they all have had attempts on their lives through anomalous means within the past three months.

+ show block
– hide block

The people are administered amnestics and are put back in their homes with a Foundation agent trailing them to make sure they are not killed. The researchers begin investigations on possible reasons why the attempted killers are targeting these people.

The Foundation intercepts a radio transmission of an unknown voice describing how the mugs failed- and how the targets were being followed by an unknown person- the Foundation agent.
The Foundation discovers the existence of a group of anomalous killers, which have been the perpetrators of an unknown amount of murders, possibly in the hundreds, since 2008.

The Foundation begins research into this unknown group, but they can only gather limited info. From what they can find, this group calls themselves the Sword of the King, and it does not seem that they know about the Foundation.

The article ends with an interrogation log in which the NYC-based Foundation agent gets information from a captured assassin. The assassin reveals that the Sword isn't the group who's after the targets. They are just hired guns, using makeshift anomalies to take down their targets without attracting suspicion. Evidently, it didn't work, because they are being tracked down and captured. Before the prisoner can speak more, he is shot and killed by another assassin who flees the scene.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The anomaly concept is fairly basic, but it was designed to be so. The real hook is the mystery and investigation into the group that is targeting these people.

Additional Notes: With this SCP, I am hoping to set up an opportunity for a new GOI or POI and more SCPs. I'm considering making this a tale instead, but I've always liked SCPs with a little more story meat on their bones. All criticism is appreciated!
